proposer.mechanism: TRADE-TICK AGGRESSOR-FLOW SKIP gate, layered on position-tier-gate (cap=1) verbatim. The exec algo subscribes to TRADE TICKS in on_start() (NOT quote ticks — see r4 lesson on quote-tick under-fire). In on_trade_tick(), maintain a rolling time-window of signed trade size: signed_size = +size if aggressor_side=BUYER, -size if aggressor_side=SELLER. Aggregate over a 3-second window (long enough to be statistically meaningful at MES trade rates of ~10-50 trades/s, short enough to be a current-flow signal). On each on_order() for an OPEN that survives the cap=1 gate, compute net_flow = sum of signed sizes in window. Compute side_aligned_flow = net_flow * side_sign (where side_sign=+1 for BUY OPEN, -1 for SELL OPEN). If side_aligned_flow <= -flow_threshold (default -3.0 contracts, i.e. the last 3s of aggressor activity was strongly AGAINST the OPEN direction), SKIP the OPEN. Otherwise SUBMIT. CLOSE (is_reduce_only=True) orders always submit unchanged. Buffer maintained as a deque pruned by ts_event timestamp at the 3s retention horizon. Safe-SUBMIT defaults if the buffer is empty or trade-tick subscription not yet established.
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: Adverse aggressor flow as a directional contra-indicator. The oracle (sigma=6.0, R^2~14%) issues a directional signal every 1s; its noise floor is high enough that when recent aggressor flow strongly disagrees with the oracle's direction, the oracle is disproportionately likely to be the noise side of the trade. Aggressor-flow-gate exists as a standalone base algo (different conditioning axis from position-tier-gate) and empirically improves the simple baseline; layering its signal as an ADDITIONAL gate after position-tier-gate's cap=1 should capture INDEPENDENT alpha because the two mechanisms condition on orthogonal axes (cap=1 = portfolio state; flow = market-flow microstructure). The trade-tick delivery channel is empirically reliable in this Nautilus simulator (verified: aggressor-flow-gate base algo works without the under-fire problem R4 hit with on_quote_tick). Expected effect: filter the subset of OPENs where the oracle is contradicted by 3 seconds of recent fill flow — those have a lower win rate (analogous to r4's adverse-tick observation but using a delivery channel that's reliable in the simulator).
proposer.why_survives_costs: Mean slippage stays 0 and commissions stay 0 in this simulator (verified from position-tier-gate backtest-results.json: mean_slippage=0.0, max_abs_slippage=0.0, total_commissions=0.0). The mechanism only adds a SKIP condition on OPEN MARKET orders — no order construction, no order modification, no new order types, no passive orders. CLOSE orders submit unchanged so intraday_flat compliance is preserved. Runtime overhead: on_trade_tick appends one tuple to a deque and prunes the left side (O(1) amortized per trade); on_order does a linear sum over the deque whose length is bounded by trade rate * 3s (typically <150 entries even in dense periods).
proposer.builds_on: position-tier-gate (cap=1 retained verbatim as the first gate; aggressor-flow filter is an additive SKIP gate applied AFTER cap=1 passes, only for OPEN orders). Different conditioning axis from prior PC runs: r1 (consensus filter) was inert; r2 (loss-cooldown) failed because losses are i.i.d. (-6.1% pnl); r3 (winners-run extend close) catastrophically failed because oracle reversal signals are real (-82%); r4 (adverse-tick-flow via quote-tick buffer) had a +13.74% offline signal that collapsed to -3.14% live because on_quote_tick under-fires in dense periods. This proposal switches to the TRADE-TICK delivery channel which is empirically reliable in this simulator (the existing aggressor-flow-gate base algo runs successfully with on_trade_tick). This makes the live behavior match the offline analysis far more closely than r4's quote-tick approach.
proposer.alternatives_considered: (1) Re-do r4's quote-tick adverse-momentum buffer with eager subscription in on_start() and use buffer's own latest entry (per r4 NOTES suggestion): the underlying issue is on_quote_tick fires only on top-of-book CHANGES not every MBP-1 msg — fixing the subscription timing doesn't fix the delivery semantics. Dropped. (2) Order-cadence-sampled adverse momentum (sample mid only at on_order time, compare to prior on_order snapshot): empirically tested via 3-date sample — at the oracle's 1Hz cadence, signed_mom_between_consecutive_OPENs is mostly zero (mid hasn't moved 1+ tick within 1s most of the time), so the threshold-based filter is INERT. The high-frequency signal r4 found at 100ms genuinely requires sub-second sampling, which isn't reliably available. (3) Session-clock-bucket filter (skip OPENs in train-aggregate-negative half-hours, +3.34% offline): the per-date check shows NO bucket has >=2/3 of dates negative — the bucket-level negative aggregates are driven by 1-2 large-loss days, not a robust signal. Overfit risk too high. (4) Skip-after-zero-prev-pnl rule: empirically tested, gives -8.5% delta — break-even prior positions are not predictive of bad next OPENs. (5) Inter-trade-gap filter (min N seconds since prior CLOSE): cap=1 already enforces gap>=1s in 100% of opens; the filter is redundant. (6) Loss-magnitude stop (r3 round 1 alternative): empirically shown losses are <=2t in 99% of cases (per r3 analysis), so a 2-tick stop saves <5%. (7) Modifying the position cap based on prior-position outcome (e.g., raise cap=2 after a winning long-hold): the oracle never holds >1 contract in the simulator regardless of cap, so this is inert (per base NOTES).

objections.text: Empirical evidence FROM A BASE ALGORITHM (read-allowed) contradicts the Proposer's additive-orthogonality claim. aggressor-flow-gate's NOTES.md reports the standalone algorithm achieves realized_pnl=$3,059.25 over the same 12-date train window (vs simple baseline $1,984.00, +54.2% PASS). But position-tier-gate alone is $4,262.50. The aggressor-flow filter REMOVES 21.6% of base 'simple' trades and yields LESS pnl than position-tier-gate's removal of ~32% of simple trades. This is direct empirical evidence that aggressor-flow-gate's skip-set is LESS PROFITABLE than position-tier-gate's skip-set for this strategy on this train window — the two filters do NOT capture orthogonal alpha; they capture overlapping or differently-weighted slices of the same noise distribution. Adding aggressor-flow on TOP of cap=1 will almost certainly remove some of the trades that cap=1 already gates around (cap=1 skips the same-ts_init CLOSE+OPEN; those concurrent skips would have been blocked anyway by aggressor flow if the flow happens to be adverse), AND will also remove trades that cap=1 KEPT (genuine post-1s entries with adverse recent flow). The Proposer has NOT measured: (a) how many additional trades the layered filter actually skips vs cap=1 alone, (b) the PnL of those incremental skips. Without this measurement, the proposal is a hopeful conjunction. Given r4's offline-vs-live divergence (+13.74% → -3.14%), the empirical bar on this experiment is now much higher than 'plausible' — it requires actual measurement.

Trade-tick delivery rate ASSUMPTION is unverified. The Proposer claims 'on_trade_tick delivery channel is empirically reliable' citing aggressor-flow-gate's PASS. But aggressor-flow-gate succeeds at +54.2% over the SIMPLE BASELINE — a much lower bar than position-tier-gate (+204.9% over simple). The standalone algo's success does NOT prove that trade-tick delivery rate is high enough to deliver the SAME signal quality when combined with cap=1's already-aggressive trade-reduction. In dense-trade periods (the regimes where aggressor-flow-gate likely sources most of its alpha), trade-tick delivery COULD be similarly throttled to quote-ticks in r4. The Proposer needs to either: (a) verify trade-tick delivery rate matches the raw MBP-1 trade stream by instrumenting on_trade_tick callback count vs raw fills, or (b) explicitly acknowledge that this is the same delivery-channel-trust issue that broke r4 and that the live result could diverge from any offline projection.

No empirical pre-validation. r4's hypothesis at least had a measured +13.74% offline before live-test; this proposal has ZERO empirical pre-validation of the layered-filter combination. The Proposer should run the offline analysis: at each base position-tier-gate OPEN (using positions.csv ts_init), join with trade ticks from the raw DBN, compute net_flow over the proposed 3s window, and measure: (a) skip count under various thresholds, (b) PnL of skipped subset, (c) per-date stability. Without this, we have no idea whether the rule's hyperparameters (3s window, -3.0 threshold) are calibrated or random. r1, r2, r3, r4 all failed in part because they lacked or had flawed pre-validation; we should not repeat that. Note also that this offline analysis IS LIKELY to show the result is worse than expected — see BLOCKING point — but doing it is the discipline this experiment lacks.

Regime fragility risk. The Proposer admits the per-date pattern is unmeasured. Given aggressor-flow-gate beats simple on 10/12 dates per its NOTES, the layered version on top of cap=1 likely has similar variance — but position-tier-gate beats simple on ALL 12 dates with much larger margins. Adding a filter on top can only either help marginally or hurt — the structural ceiling for improvement is limited because base position-tier-gate is already capturing the dominant edge. The Proposer's expected effect is asserted vaguely ('lower win rate subset') without quantification or per-date stability analysis. Combined with the +5% gate, the realistic outcome distribution is concentrated near 0%, with tail risk on both sides.

Superior alternative not considered: ABANDON the layering approach entirely. Four runs in this experiment have failed to beat position-tier-gate. The empirical record strongly suggests position-tier-gate is at a local optimum and incremental filters do not help. A materially different mechanism would be: RANDOMIZED REDUCTION (sample-and-deduplicate). Instead of trying to predict which OPENs will fail, randomly drop X% of cap=1-passing OPENs to reduce variance — this would test whether the base algo's pnl is sensitive to volume or whether per-trade pnl is high enough that random subsampling preserves expected pnl. If random sampling preserves pnl with lower variance, that's a Sharpe improvement (since variance drops faster than expected return) — Sharpe is part of the refinement gate. The mechanism's expected behavior: if position-tier-gate has E[pnl/trade]=$0.047 with variance V, random 50% sampling preserves E[pnl/trade] but reduces total variance by 50% — Sharpe could rise meaningfully. This is the clearest UNTRIED orthogonal mechanism in the experiment. The Proposer should at minimum explain why this isn't worth trying.

Window=3s and threshold=-3.0 are unmotivated. aggressor-flow-gate uses window=10s, threshold=2.0. The Proposer chose 3s/3.0 without empirical basis. The 3s window may be too short to give a stable flow signal at low-trade-rate periods (Asia hours, weekend overnight).

Buffer-population timing on first call. The proposal subscribes 'in on_start()' but doesn't verify that on_start is called before the first on_order. Per the standard Nautilus lifecycle, on_start fires when the algo is started before backtest run, so this is fine, but should be documented.

suggested_alternatives: RANDOMIZED REDUCTION: randomly drop X% of cap=1-passing OPENs (e.g. X=30%). Hypothesis: per-trade expected pnl is uniform enough that random sampling preserves mean while reducing variance, improving Sharpe. Untried in this experiment.

Pre-validate the layered aggressor-flow hypothesis OFFLINE: at each base PTG OPEN (ts_init), compute net_flow from raw DBN trade prints over the 3s window. Report (i) % of cap-passing OPENs that would be additionally skipped, (ii) PnL of incremental skips, (iii) per-date stability. If incremental skip PnL is NOT clearly net-negative, the hypothesis is dead before implementation.

If proceeding with aggressor-flow: use the SAME parameters as the working standalone aggressor-flow-gate (window=10s, threshold=2.0) rather than newly-invented ones. Reduces parameter-search overfitting risk.
criticizer.reasoning: BLOCKING: the cited evidence (aggressor-flow-gate standalone pnl=$3059 < position-tier-gate $4262) shows the two filters are NOT obviously additive — combining them has substantial structural risk of subtraction. The proposal lacks the offline pre-validation that r4 at least attempted, and is suggesting hyperparameters without empirical basis. After 4 prior failed runs in this experiment, the Criticizer should demand empirical pre-validation before any implementation, OR a structurally novel mechanism (like randomized reduction) that doesn't rely on layered-filter additivity.

proposer.mechanism: REPRODUCE-AND-FIX r4 (adverse-tick-flow): re-implement r4's hypothesis with the two specific fixes called out in r4's own NOTES.md 'Suggested next attempt': (1) Subscribe to quote ticks EAGERLY in on_start() using a hard-coded MESM6 instrument_id (not lazily on first order — this lets the buffer warm up before the first OPEN). (2) Replace the cache.quote_tick(instrument_id) call for mid_now with reading the buffer's own LATEST entry (guarantees algorithm-internal consistency between the 'now' and 'now-100ms' quotes — eliminates the source of the live-vs-offline divergence). The rest of the algorithm is identical to r4: deque of (ts_event_ns, mid, spread) populated in on_quote_tick(); on each OPEN that survives cap=1, compute signed_mom_100 = (mid_now - mid_100ms_ago) / TICK_SIZE * side_sign; compute spread_ticks = (ask - bid) / TICK_SIZE from the buffer's latest entry; if signed_mom_100 <= -1.0 AND spread_ticks <= 1.0, SKIP. Buffer pruning at 200ms retention. Same TICK_SIZE=0.25. CLOSE orders submit unchanged.
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: Same as r4: in tight-spread regimes (modal MES state), a sharp 100ms adverse mid move BEFORE the OPEN signals the oracle is reacting to a transient price excursion that has already partially mean-reverted. The offline analysis showed +13.74% on the train window when the lookup was done correctly via bisect_right on the raw MBP-1 quote stream. R4's LIVE failure (-3.14%) is hypothesized in r4's own NOTES to be caused by on_quote_tick under-firing (delivery is throttled to top-of-book CHANGES rather than every MBP-1 message) AND the inconsistency between cache.quote_tick() (which returns SOME latest quote, possibly stale or mis-aligned with on_quote_tick deliveries) and the buffer's own contents. The two fixes target exactly these issues: (a) eager subscription removes any race between subscribe time and first OPEN; (b) using buffer's own latest entry for mid_now removes the cache-vs-buffer inconsistency. If on_quote_tick DOES fire frequently enough to populate the buffer in dense periods, the offline-projected uplift should materialize. If it doesn't, we will see a similar small regression as r4 (bounded downside).
proposer.why_survives_costs: Mean slippage stays 0 and commissions stay 0 in this simulator (verified). Only adds a SKIP condition on OPEN MARKET orders. CLOSE orders submit unchanged so intraday_flat compliance is preserved. Runtime overhead is negligible (deque ops + bisect).
proposer.builds_on: position-tier-gate (cap=1 retained verbatim). DIRECT FIX of r4 (-3.14%) per its own documented next-attempt suggestion. NOT a layering of two filters — same single mechanism as r4 with the two specific implementation fixes. Other PC runs (r1, r2, r3, r5-round-1) have all been REJECTED for various structural reasons; this is the one path that has BOTH (a) an empirically measured offline uplift signal (+13.74%) and (b) a specific implementation hypothesis for WHY live differed (the buffer+cache inconsistency).
proposer.alternatives_considered: (1) Round-1 trade-tick aggressor flow on top of cap=1: BLOCKING-validated empirically via the criticizer-demanded offline pre-validation on 3 late-train dates (20260318-20260320). Result: ALL thresholds (-0 to -100 contracts) produce DELTA in range [-15%, -42%] — i.e. the skip-subset has POSITIVE pnl (+$646 over 23,511 trades when adv_10s<=0), meaning the rule removes PROFITABLE trades rather than losers. The criticizer's BLOCKING was correct. This empirically dies. (2) Randomized/deterministic decimation (criticizer's alt): tested via offline on full train — keep-every-Nth and random-fraction-drop reduce pnl roughly proportional to trade count (e.g. keep 50% → -47% pnl, daily Sharpe roughly preserved at ~18 vs base 18.4, NOT improved). The 'variance shrinks faster than mean' hypothesis is FALSE in this dataset — per-trade pnl is approximately uniform, so subsampling preserves both mean and Sharpe. Declined. (3) Inverse aggressor-flow filter (skip when flow IS WITH direction = contrarian preference): offline shows the adv_10s>0 half also has positive pnl ($1025 over 22669 trades, mean $0.045 vs adv_10s<=0 mean $0.027). Both halves are net-positive — there's no clean half to drop. Declined. (4) Loss-pnl-history, sign-churn, session-clock-bucket filters: ALL empirically tested offline, ALL produce -1% to -45% delta. None robust. Declined. (5) Position-cap=2 instead of 1: per base NOTES, the oracle never holds >1 contract, so cap=2 is structurally inert (delta=0). Declined. (6) Spawning passive limits / passive maker variants: r2-round-1 BLOCKING (adverse-selection inversion). Declined.
proposer.revision_notes: Round 1 BLOCKING (layered-filter additivity false): VALIDATED EMPIRICALLY via offline pre-validation on 3 late-train dates per criticizer demand. The criticizer was correct — layered aggressor-flow REMOVES profitable trades and is dead. Round 1 MAJOR (trade-tick delivery rate assumption): MOOT — the layered hypothesis is dead regardless. Round 1 MAJOR (no empirical pre-validation): ADDRESSED — pre-validation is now done and the original hypothesis is rejected; the pivoted hypothesis (r4 fix) HAS the +13.74% offline signal from r4. Round 1 MAJOR (regime fragility): same as r4's documented per-date concern. Round 1 MAJOR (superior alternative - randomized reduction): TESTED EMPIRICALLY and rejected — pnl drops proportionally with trade count, no Sharpe benefit. Round 1 MINOR (window/threshold not motivated): MOOT — pivoted hypothesis uses r4's calibrated parameters (100ms window, -1.0 threshold, 1-tick spread gate).

objections.text: The two proposed 'fixes' may not actually address the root cause of r4's failure. r4's NOTES.md observed the LIVE buffer fired ~10-15x less often than the offline analysis predicted (e.g. on 20260316: 154 live skips vs 2400 analysis-predicted). The Proposer hypothesizes this is due to: (a) lazy vs eager subscription, and (b) cache-vs-buffer inconsistency. But r4's NOTES.md explicitly listed a third hypothesis the Proposer is NOT addressing: 'on_quote_tick fires only for top-of-book CHANGES, not every MBP-1 message — so the buffer has far fewer entries than the offline analysis assumes.' If this third hypothesis is the actual cause, then eager subscription and buffer-self-consistency do NOTHING — the buffer is STRUCTURALLY missing the 90% of MBP-1 quote messages that don't change top-of-book. The Proposer should explicitly state which of these three hypotheses is being addressed and why the other(s) are unlikely. Without this, we're flying blind on whether the live fix will recover the offline signal.

If hypothesis (c) - 'on_quote_tick fires on TOB-changes-only' - is the cause, then BOTH the proposed fixes are inert and the algorithm will produce essentially the same -3.14% result as r4. The Proposer should EITHER: (i) instrument the live algo with a counter (log every Nth on_quote_tick call, compare callback count to expected MBP-1 rate offline) BEFORE committing to the fix; (ii) propose a fallback mechanism that doesn't depend on the quote-tick callback rate (e.g., use a longer lookback window of 1-5 seconds that doesn't require sub-second tick density; but per the Proposer's own data this gives only +2.72% which is below the gate); (iii) try `subscribe_order_book_deltas` instead — book deltas may fire more frequently than top-of-book changes (every level update). Otherwise the run has a high probability of being a near-replica of r4's failure.

Decision-time staleness: even if the buffer is populated correctly, using 'buffer's own latest entry' for mid_now means the algo's view of 'now' is the LATEST QUOTE DELIVERED to on_quote_tick — which could be milliseconds-to-seconds old if the engine delivered the order on_order callback before the next quote_tick delivery. The Proposer should specify: at on_order, what's the typical lag between the buffer's latest ts_event and the order's ts_init? If it's >100ms (the lookback horizon), the entire signal is corrupted — mid_now is actually older than mid_100ms_ago should have been. Per Nautilus message-bus ordering this lag should be 0 in a deterministic backtest replay, but the assertion needs verification. Add an assertion: if buffer_latest_ts > order.ts_init, fall back to SUBMIT (defensive). If buffer_latest_ts < order.ts_init - 100ms, also fall back to SUBMIT (stale-data guard) — this would make the divergence between live and offline measurable and bounded.

Instrument_id hard-coding: the Proposer says 'hard-coded MESM6 instrument_id' in on_start. Need to verify the InstrumentId constructor (from nautilus_trader.model.identifiers) accepts a string like 'MESM6.GLBX' or just 'MESM6'. R4 used lazy subscription which deferred this problem; the eager version needs a concrete instrument_id at on_start time. Specify either the full venue-qualified id or derive it from config.

The Proposer's offline pre-validation for the round-1 (layered aggressor-flow) hypothesis is valuable and the empirical refutation is convincing. This is a discipline improvement over r1/r2/r3 (which lacked pre-validation) and r4 (which had pre-validation but didn't carry the discipline forward at debug time). The pivoted hypothesis (r4 fix) inherits the offline +13.74% number from r4's own pre-validation, so the discipline is preserved. Acceptable.

suggested_alternatives: Add INSTRUMENTATION to the live algo: count on_quote_tick callbacks per session and emit a log line with the count at session end. The count compared to the raw MBP-1 quote rate would diagnose whether on_quote_tick is fully or partially delivered. If the count is <10% of the raw rate, hypothesis (c) is confirmed and the algo should fall back to SUBMIT (rather than try to use a structurally-missing signal).

If the live test shows the same under-fire pattern as r4: this experiment has now exhausted every reasonable hypothesis on the position-tier-gate axis. The run-5 result would be informational rather than passing.
objections.reasoning: The pivot to fix-r4 is logically coherent and empirically grounded (uses r4's measured +13.74% offline signal), but two of the three hypotheses for r4's failure are NOT addressed by the proposed fixes (eager subscription, buffer-self-consistency). If the actual cause is on_quote_tick TOB-only firing, this run is a near-replica of r4. The Proposer should EITHER specify why on_quote_tick will fire often enough OR add instrumentation to MEASURE the callback rate during the live run, OR specify a structural fallback (e.g., abort the SKIP decision when the buffer is sparser than expected). Without these guards, the run is uninformative.
